# Glacier coherence through the seasons

This tutorial computes coherence for one 12-day pair per month over the
Aletsch glacier in 2022. Coherence shows where the surface stayed the same
between two acquisitions, so it separates moving ice and changing snow from
ground that stays put.


## Process one pair per month

The search is the same as in the [backscatter tutorial](glacier-backscatter.qmd).
`find_pairs()` forms every pair of acquisitions 12 days apart; keeping the
first pair of each month leaves twelve, which are processed into coherence:

::: {#0c6331e0 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from s1bursts import BurstCatalog, BurstProcessor, CoherenceConfig, FileManager, SearchQuery, TimeRange
from s1bursts.burst import BurstPairCollection

fm = FileManager("data/glacier")
catalog = BurstCatalog(fm)
bursts = catalog.search(SearchQuery(
    time_range=TimeRange("2022-01-01", "2022-12-31"),
    burst_id=30346, sub_swath="IW1", polarization="VV",
))

df = bursts.find_pairs(baseline=12).df.sort_values("date_1")
monthly = BurstPairCollection(df.groupby(df.date_1.dt.month).head(1))
print(f"{len(monthly)} pairs selected")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
12 pairs selected
```
:::
:::


::: {#cbe2a2a9 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
catalog.download(monthly).raise_on_failure()
processor = BurstProcessor(fm)
coherence = processor.create_coherences(
    monthly, crs="auto", config=CoherenceConfig(grid_spacing=20),
).raise_on_failure()
```
:::


## Map coherence in winter and summer

The maps compare a winter pair with a summer pair. In January almost the whole
area is incoherent, because snowfall and wind change the snow surface between
the two dates. In August the ice-free slopes are highly coherent, while the
glacier stays dark, which makes its outline stand out.

::: {#d839eedd .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import rasterio
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds
from shapely.geometry import box

view = (7.95, 46.38, 8.15, 46.55)  # lon/lat bounds of the map
areas = {
    "glacier": (box(8.065, 46.472, 8.072, 46.477), "white"),
    "ice-free ground": (box(8.104, 46.448, 8.112, 46.453), "tab:cyan"),
}
products = sorted(coherence.products, key=lambda p: p.date_primary)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.8, 3.7), sharey=True, layout="constrained")
for ax, product in zip(axes, [products[0], products[7]]):
    with rasterio.open(fm.get_product_path(product)) as src:
        left, bottom, right, top = transform_bounds("EPSG:4326", src.crs, *view)
        coh = src.read(1, window=from_bounds(left, bottom, right, top, src.transform))
        for area, color in areas.values():
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = transform_bounds("EPSG:4326", src.crs, *area.bounds)
            ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((x0 / 1000, y0 / 1000), (x1 - x0) / 1000,
                                       (y1 - y0) / 1000, fill=False, edgecolor=color))
    image = ax.imshow(coh, extent=[v / 1000 for v in (left, right, bottom, top)],
                      cmap="magma", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    ax.set(title=f"{product.date_primary:%d %b} to {product.date_secondary:%d %b %Y}", xlabel="Easting (km)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Northing (km)")
fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, shrink=0.8, label="Coherence")
plt.show()
```

:::

## Follow coherence through the year

The time series takes the median coherence of each pair within the two
rectangles, one on the glacier and one on an ice-free slope east of it.

::: {#f600769c .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rasterio.mask import mask
from rasterio.warp import transform_geom
from shapely.geometry import mapping

records = []
for product in products:
    with rasterio.open(fm.get_product_path(product)) as src:
        for name, (area, _) in areas.items():
            region = transform_geom("EPSG:4326", src.crs, mapping(area))
            values, _ = mask(src, [region], indexes=1, crop=True, filled=False)
            valid = values.compressed()
            records.append({"date": product.date_primary, "area": name,
                            "coherence": np.median(valid[np.isfinite(valid)])})
series = pd.DataFrame(records).pivot(index="date", columns="area", values="coherence")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.8, 3.3))
for name, (_, color) in areas.items():
    ax.plot(series.index, series[name], "o-", label=name,
            color="tab:blue" if color == "white" else color)
ax.set(xlabel="Date of the first acquisition", ylabel="Median coherence", ylim=(0, 1))
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.autofmt_xdate()
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Median coherence of one 12-day pair per month in 2022, on the glacier and on ice-free ground.](glacier-coherence_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=649 height=308}
:::
:::


## Interpret the result

On the glacier, coherence stays near 0.12 all year. Values this low mean that
the two acquisitions are essentially unrelated; an estimate from a finite window
of pixels cannot reach exactly 0. The glacier flows, and its surface melts or
gains new snow, so 12 days are too long for it to stay coherent.

On the ice-free ground, coherence follows the snow cover. It is low from
November to May, rises in June, and stays between 0.57 and 0.74 until October,
when the snow returns. Summer coherence therefore separates ice-free ground
from glacier ice, even where both look similar in backscatter.

Shorter baselines keep more coherence. In 2022 only Sentinel-1A was operating,
so 12 days is the shortest baseline available for these dates.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
